# `exec lock` on a path someone else holds used to block FOREVER: no --wait to opt
# out of, no --timeout to bound it, no flag of any kind — the exact opposite of
# `acquire lock`, which fails fast by default and has both. For an agent wrapping a
# build in `exec lock`, that's a hung session with nothing to act on.
#
# It now fails fast like `acquire lock`, blocks only when asked (--wait), and can be
# bounded (--timeout). A lock conflict also exits 4 rather than the generic 1, so a
# script can tell "someone else has it, try later" apart from "your command is
# wrong, it will fail identically forever."
env BREEZE_DIR=$WORK/state

exec breeze register identity a
exec breeze register identity b

exec touch contended.txt
exec touch free.txt
exec breeze acquire lock contended.txt --as a
stdout 'l1'

# --- exec lock: fails fast instead of hanging ---
exec sh -c 'breeze exec lock contended.txt --as b -- /bin/echo built; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'exit=4'
stderr 'already held by "a"'
! stdout 'built'

# --try is the same behavior, said out loud at the call site
exec sh -c 'breeze exec lock contended.txt --try --as b -- /bin/echo built; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'exit=4'

# --wait is now available, and --timeout bounds it (this used to be unbounded with
# no way to express either)
exec sh -c 'breeze exec lock contended.txt --wait --timeout 1s --as b -- /bin/echo built; echo exit=$?'
stderr 'timed out waiting for lock'
stdout 'exit=4'

# an uncontended path is unaffected — the command runs and the lock is released
exec sh -c 'breeze exec lock free.txt --as b -- /bin/echo built; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'built'
stdout 'exit=0'

# --- acquire lock: the conflict exit code a try-lock needs ---
exec sh -c 'breeze acquire lock contended.txt --as b; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'exit=4'

# a NON-conflict failure keeps the generic 1, which is the whole point of the
# distinction: retrying this one would fail identically forever
exec sh -c 'breeze acquire lock --as b; echo exit=$?'
stdout 'exit=1'

# the branch a script actually writes
exec sh -c 'if breeze acquire lock contended.txt --as b >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo got-it; elif [ $? -eq 4 ]; then echo busy-skipping; else echo real-error; fi'
stdout 'busy-skipping'

# --- contradictory flags are named, not silently resolved ---
exec sh -c 'breeze acquire lock free.txt --try --wait --as b; echo exit=$?'
stderr 'opposites'
stdout 'exit=1'

# a timeout with nothing to time out never does what it looks like it does
exec sh -c 'breeze acquire lock free.txt --timeout 5s --as b; echo exit=$?'
stderr 'only applies with --wait'
stdout 'exit=1'

# --- --wait actually gets the lock once the holder releases it ---
exec breeze release locks --as a
exec breeze acquire lock contended.txt --wait --timeout 5s --as b
stdout 'l\d'

exec breeze stop
